fields.help: TCP port llama-server listens on, on this machine only (127.0.0.1) — never exposed to your network. The default 8080 is fine unless something else on your system is already using it; any free port from 1-65535 works.
fields.label: Port

fields.help: Maximum number of tokens (roughly, word-pieces) of conversation llama.cpp keeps in memory at once — prompt plus reply combined. Bigger means it remembers more of a long chat/document, but uses more RAM/VRAM and can respond slower. Typical values: 2048-4096 for short chats, 8192-16384 for longer ones, 32768+ only for large documents on machines with memory to spare.
fields.label: Context size

fields.help: How many of the model's layers to run on the GPU instead of the CPU. 999 (default) offloads every layer llama.cpp can — fastest, if the model fits in your GPU's VRAM. 0 = CPU only. If Start crashes or the log shows an out-of-memory error, the model likely doesn't fit in VRAM — try a smaller number (e.g. 20-40) to offload only part of it, or 0 to fall back to CPU entirely.
fields.label: GPU layers

fields.help: Override the auto-detected llama-server executable — point this at a custom build (e.g. a different backend, or a newer version), or paste a direct download URL to a release archive (.zip/.tar.gz) to fetch and install it automatically. Leave blank to use the bundled/auto-detected one.
fields.hint: Local binary path or a download URL...
fields.label: llama-server binary

fields.help:
Appended verbatim to the llama-server command, after the built-in options (port/context size/GPU layers). Space-separated; wrap a value containing spaces in "double quotes". An invalid or unsupported flag will make the server fail to start — check the log pane at the bottom of the main window if Start doesn't work.

Examples:
--threads 8         number of CPU threads to use
--flash-attn on     enable flash attention (faster; needs support)
--batch-size 512    tokens processed per batch
--no-mmap           disable memory-mapping the model file
--rope-freq-base 0  override RoPE frequency base (long-context models)
fields.label: Extra command-line arguments

fields.help: Variables for llama-server, one KEY=VALUE per line; a line that starts with # is a comment. Most of its options can be given this way as well as on the command line: LLAMA_ARG_THREADS=8 is --threads 8 (when both are given, the command line wins). The graphics libraries take only variables, e.g. GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 to use the first GPU alone with a Vulkan build. LD_LIBRARY_PATH is QuickAI's: it points at the build's own libraries.
fields.label: Extra environment (KEY=VALUE per line)

fields.help: Where models fetched via the "Model" box (download/import/search) or "Look up online" are saved and read back from. The models bundled with the app itself live in their own read-only folder regardless of this.
fields.label: Downloaded models folder
